newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi River reopened at barge accident site.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi River reopened at barge accident site.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard on Wednesday said the Mississippi River was reopened to one-way traffic past the site near here where a barge accident had closed the river since Monday.

"We have an officer on board a commercial tug to serve as the gatekeeper for traffic on the river and vessels will be allowed to proceed with his permission one at a time, one way at a time," Coast Guard Commander Ken Parris told Reuters.
The river was shut Monday evening when a tugboat with 25 barges in tow struck a bridge, sinking two barges and capsizing a barge carrying a volatile mix of gasoline and benzene.
Other tugs operating on the river nearby scrambled to round up barges that broke loose, and one remained missing, the Coast Guard said.

Divers were working to attached hoses to the capsized barge to begin lightering operations to empty its contents. Once that is completed, the barge will be uprighted by two large cranes brought upriver from New Orleans, the Coast Guard said.
The backlog of river traffic Wednesday included two passenger river boats with more than 700 people on board and 20 tows handling an undetermined number of barges.
